Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We had a couple questions from procurement and security as we move toward PO: primarily around private VPC hosting, data residency, and audit rights. High level asks from our side:

- VPC-only hosting with data residency in the US (no cross-border replication).
- Ability to run one annual third-party audit (external auditor) with access to logs and relevant configuration; procurement expects a written audit scope and timeframe.
- Confirmation on whether Redwood will accept our external auditor (we typically use NewLeaf Audit Services).
- Commercial: EdgeNet is requesting a one-time 25% discount as part of an accelerated 12-mo prepay.

Procurement is on a tight timeline and has requested final terms by end of week (Aug 20) to meet their procurement cycle. Can you confirm what is feasible and whether any of these items require exec sign-off?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,

EdgeNet Inc

Sara —

Thanks for the detail and the clear timeline. High-level responses now, specifics below and we will loop Legal & Deal Desk.

- VPC hosting + US-only residency: yes, we can host in a customer VPC with data residency constrained to a single US region. We will include the residency clause in the SOW and infra diagram.
- Audit: we typically allow one annual third-party audit with pre-approved scope. Full production access is rare — we provide logs, config exports, and evidence. On-prem or direct production access requires a separate process and is usually declined.
- External auditor acceptance: Redwood will accept accredited third-party auditors subject to a short pre-approval questionnaire and agreed scope.
- Discount: I noted the 25% request. This is a non-standard commercial concession and will need deal desk / exec approval.

Next steps I propose: Aditya, can you attach the SOW stub and a proposed redline for the audit clause? Laura, I will route this to Deal Desk and request exec clearance. Rishi / Markus — we need a decision on the commercial ask and any carveouts for the audit language.

Recommendation: approve a commercial compromise and a narrowly-scoped audit carveout to keep the deal moving. Specifics for approval:

1) Discount: approve up to 20% one-time prepay credit (not 25%). Finance can treat this as a credit note applied on execution.

3) Residency: US-only region enforcement in the SOW and infra diagram; no cross-region backups containing customer data.

Conditions: Legal signoff required on the redlined audit clause and indemnity carveouts; exec sign-off (Markus) needed for the commercial concession. Please confirm by EOD Tue Aug 18 to meet EdgeNet timeline.
